cross_references.note: ADA Title II violation (42 USC §12132) is a per se CIV §51 violation under §51(f) and a per se CIV §54 violation under §54(c). Establishing ADA Title II triggers California statutory damages ($4,000/$1,000 minimum per offense) automatically. ADA Title II analysis is the federal predicate; Unruh/Disabled Persons Act is the California remedy.

ADA Title I violation (42 USC §12112) is a per se Unruh violation under §51(f). However, for employment discrimination, the FEHA track (§12940 + CRD exhaustion) is the primary California vehicle. Unruh applies to employment discrimination at 'business establishments' — but it supplements rather than replaces the FEHA employment track.

FEHA §12940 requires CRD administrative exhaustion; Unruh/CIV §51 does not. In disability discrimination cases, both tracks should be pled: FEHA for the employment track (with exhaustion); Unruh for the business establishment access track (without exhaustion). They are separate causes of action.

Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act (29 USC §794) covers programs receiving federal financial assistance. State courts, hospitals, and schools receiving federal funds are covered. A §504 violation may also constitute an ADA violation → per se Unruh violation under §51(f). The §504 track is the federal funding-recipient vehicle; Unruh is the California enforcement vehicle.

Health plan denial of medically necessary care to a disabled person may constitute both a Knox-Keene Act violation (HSC §1340 framework) and a Unruh Civil Rights Act violation (CIV §51) if the denial is disability-based. Knox-Keene is the insurance regulatory track; Unruh is the civil rights track. Both may apply to the same denial.
